prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Create ONE portrait of ISAKA's fictional chosen dark-haired cup-holder avatar reimagined as an ADULT space-western field-radio engineer in a 1950s American pulp science-fiction illustration. Input1 supplies only the motifs dark tousled hair, gentle expression, dark clothing, coffee cup. It is an illustrated account avatar, not a photo of the owner. Inputs2 and3 supply mid-century printed comic/pulp visual language and NATURALLY PROPORTIONED ADULT HUMAN FACE construction. Use the male space adventurer's mature facial proportions, small eyes, substantial nose, adult jaw, hand-inked creases and gouache planes as the approach to anatomy, but create an original adult character, not that reference man's exact likeness. Short messy black hair, thoughtful normal-sized dark eyes, slight relaxed smile. Strong normal human brow-to-eye-to-nose proportions. NO anime, manga, giant eyes, baby face, soft chibi features or photographic collage.

EQUIPMENT AND COSTUME MUST BE ORIGINAL AND ASYMMETRICAL. He is a frontier communications specialist at a dusty rocket-depot workbench. Deep navy and teal canvas work coveralls with rolled cuffs, supple worn cognac leather utility harness crossing chest, thick brass belt hardware, unmarked steel coffee flask at waist. A single enormous graphics-card FIELD CASE hangs at one hip/back on the leather harness: roughly half his height, gigantic single exposed turbine-like cooling fan, jutting aluminum heatsink fins, green circuit-board edges, arched copper coolant tubes, thick braided cables. Mounted onto the case is a bizarre tall but compact folding radio mast with two oval dish reflectors and a loop aerial. An oversized cream enamel radio console is carried at lower chest on leather straps, with great rotary tuning wheels, glowing vacuum tubes, round amber analog meters and a multicolored ARC square-grid screen. One gloved hand turns a tuning wheel; other holds the sealed coffee flask. The apparatus has practical straps, brackets and plausible weight.

His face hardware is distinct: a riveted brass half-headband, ONE heavy left-ear radio receiver with a coiled cable plugged into collar, a cheek-mounted pivoting microphone, and a tiny round magnifying CRT monocular mounted above one eyebrow on an articulated arm, lowered partly over one eye. Other eye and rest of face clearly visible. NO square eyepatch, bubble helmet, scarf, identical shoulder packs, twin upright triple-fan pillars or red/cream pressure suit. All equipment physically joined, anatomy and lighting coherent. No giant generic medieval armor.

Show head through hips in a dynamic three-quarter portrait, body slightly angled at workbench, all headgear/mast and essential apparatus contained. Dusty red-orange rock mesas and slender tail-fin rockets through open depot arch, a pale ringed planet above, small square ARC-grid work screens inside. Mix space-western working frontier with big playful compute obsession. Printed color palette teal, navy, leather brown, amber, cream, orange-red background. Strong black brush contours and crosshatching, beautiful hand-painted gouache shadows, halftone texture, subtle offset print and warm paper grain. Authentic vintage pulp adventure illustration, earnest optimism and slightly absurd engineering; no glossy 3D rendering. Make the overall silhouette, pose, backdrop, props and equipment unmistakably different from a matching uniform set.

Portrait5:7, ideally1500x2100, full bleed, head around upper third, calmer dark lower edge for optional stats later. No text, letters, numbers, names, logos, captions, speech balloons, titles, watermark, frame or border. One character only.

review: One adult illustrated frontier radio engineer with normal human proportions. Tousled dark hair and sealed flask preserve own-avatar motifs. Distinct asymmetrical single-fan GPU field case, twin dishes and loop antenna, leather harness, valve radio and round forehead optical instrument. Painted/inked pulp texture coherent across face and machinery. No scarf, anime treatment, text or card border. Earlier twin-GPU version retained as superseded draft.
commissionAuthority: Boss requested the first fixed-up anime avatar in the accepted retro-futuristic direction, then expressly required varied space-western equipment.
archiveNote: Exact native original preserved. This is a fictional avatar adaptation, not an asserted human likeness.
